core_obligations: Fix the test field: start with the connectedness of the base change X_{kbar} to a separable algebraic closure kbar of k, and let k'/k be an arbitrary field extension, which is what has to be shown to give a connected X_{k'} (proof lines 801-802).

Enlarge to a field containing both: choose a field extension kbar' of kbar into which k' embeds as an extension of k, so that the base changes of X over kbar' dominate both X_{kbar} and X_{k'} (proof lines 803-804).

Apply the separably closed case and descend: by the separably closed version of the criterion X_{kbar'} is connected, and since the base change morphism X_{kbar'} -> X_{k'} is surjective, X_{k'} is connected; as k' was arbitrary, X is geometrically connected over k, which is the asserted equivalence (proof lines 805-808).
proof_roadmap: Assume X_{kbar} is connected for a separable algebraic closure kbar and take an arbitrary field extension k'/k (proof lines 801-802).
Choose an extension kbar' of kbar containing k', so that all base changes can be compared at once (proof lines 803-804).

Use the separably closed-field version to get X_{kbar'} connected, then push connectedness down to X_{k'} along the surjective base change morphism, which proves the statement for arbitrary k' (proof lines 805-808).
difficulty_reason: The lemma replaces the a priori testing field for geometric connectedness by a single one: for a scheme X over a field k and a separable algebraic closure kbar, X is geometrically connected exactly when X_{kbar} is connected (statement lines 793-797). The forward direction is built into the definition, so the work is the converse, where an arbitrary test extension k' has to be compared with kbar: a further extension kbar' of kbar containing k' is produced, the separably closed-field criterion gives connectedness of X_{kbar'}, and connectedness is then pushed down to X_{k'} because X_{kbar'} -> X_{k'} is surjective (proof lines 803-807). The claim is H2: one comparison field, one surjectivity, and a single cited criterion.
